definitions.explanation: The dead body of an animal or insect, viewed as a physical object. For humans, it is harsh and clinical; the neutral term is {遺体|いたい}.

examples.english: There was a dead cat in the road.

examples.japanese: ⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{死骸|しがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{掃|は}いて→掃く：04260_haku⟧⟦{捨|す}てた→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧。
examples.english: I swept up the insect carcasses and threw them out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{海岸|かいがん}→海岸：00852_kaigan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{打|う}ち{上|あ}げられた→打ち上げる：06732_uchiageru⟧⟦{鯨|くじら}→鯨：04310_kujira⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{死骸|しがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発見|はっけん}→発見：00085_hakken⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A whale carcass washed ashore was discovered on the beach.

notes:
Most often used for animals and insects. When applied to humans, it sounds cold or callous, the way "carcass" does in English.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{死骸|しがい}: animal carcass
- {死骸|しがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{処理|しょり}する→処理する：25531_shorisuru⟧: to dispose of a carcass
- {死骸|しがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発見|はっけん}する→発見する：26929_hakkensuru⟧: to discover a corpse

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{遺体|いたい}→遺体：14433_itai⟧: body (of a deceased person) — neutral and respectful
- ⟦{死体|したい}→死体：04032_shitai⟧: corpse — more clinical; used in police and medical contexts for humans or animals
- ⟦{亡骸|なきがら}→亡骸：11723_nakigara⟧: mortal remains — literary and respectful, only for humans
